messages.content: You are a patient Rust tutor.
I want to learn Rust for systems work. Where should I start?
Start with the official book, then write small command-line programs. Learn ownership and borrowing first, because most other Rust features depend on them.
How long does ownership usually take to understand?
Most people need a few weeks of practice. Reading the compiler errors carefully helps a lot, since they usually name the exact borrow that conflicts.
What is the difference between a String and a &str?
A String owns its bytes and can grow. A &str is a borrowed view of UTF-8 bytes owned by someone else, often a String or a string literal.
Should I use clone to make the compiler happy?
Sometimes it is fine, but treat it as a signal to check the design. Cloning large data in a hot loop costs time, so consider borrowing or restructuring first.
Can you explain lifetimes in one paragraph?
A lifetime names how long a reference is valid. The compiler uses lifetimes to prove that no reference outlives the value it points to, so you rarely write them in simple code.
What crates would you suggest for a command-line tool?
For argument parsing, clap is the usual choice. For error handling in applications, anyhow works well, and thiserror helps when you define library error types.
How do I write a unit test?
Put a function marked with the test attribute inside a test module in the same file, and use assert_eq to compare values. Run them with cargo test.
What about integration tests?
Put them in the tests directory at the crate root. Each file there is compiled as its own crate and can use only the public interface of your library.
My program panics with index out of bounds. What should I check?
Print the length and the index just before the access. Most of the time the loop bound is off by one, or the input was shorter than the code assumed.
Is unsafe code something a beginner should write?
Not yet. Read unsafe code when you meet it, learn what invariants it relies on, and leave writing it until you can justify each invariant in a comment.
How do threads and channels work together?
A thread runs a closure, and a channel carries messages between threads. The sender moves a value into the channel and the receiver takes it out, so no data is shared unsafely.
What is the difference between Arc and Rc?
Both count references. Rc is cheap and single-threaded; Arc uses atomic counts and can be shared across threads, so it costs a little more.
How should I structure a medium-sized project?
Use a library crate for the logic and a thin binary crate for the command line. Keep modules small, and put the types that cross module boundaries in one place.
Which formatter and linter should I run?
Run rustfmt for formatting and clippy for lints. Add both to your continuous integration so that style questions never reach code review.
How do I read a file line by line?
Open it with std fs File, wrap it in a BufReader, and iterate over its lines. Each line is a Result, so use the question mark operator to propagate errors.
Is there a way to parse JSON without writing a struct for each shape?
Yes. serde_json can parse into a generic value type. Use it when the shape varies, and derive structs when the shape is fixed, since structs give you checked fields.
What about async code?
Async functions return futures that a runtime such as tokio drives. Start with blocking code, and add async only where waiting on network or disk dominates the program.
How do I profile a slow program?
Build with debug symbols in release mode, then record a profile with perf or Instruments and read the hottest functions first. Measure before and after every change.
Should I learn macros early?
Not early. Declarative macros are useful once you see repeated code you cannot remove with functions or generics. Procedural macros can wait until you need them.
What is a good first project to build?
A small tool that you would use yourself, such as a file renamer or a log filter. Keep its scope small, add tests, and publish it once it works.
